blocked_what: python3 scripts/card_claim.py --selftest run by hand from a shell -- the first four cases red at 8393d579, before today's edits

A selftest whose answer depends on its caller is testing the caller
fix_applied: pid=os.getpid() on every in-process acquire; this process is python by construction. The shell-refusal behaviour keeps its own dedicated world built with a real shell. 28/28 from both parents

supersedes_cause: regenerated by the pre-commit hook on every commit
now_known: MEASURED 2026-09-03 16:4xZ (local 09-04): two mechanisms, neither of which is 'the hook regenerates it'. A path-scoped commit could not stage it because git commit -- <paths> builds a temporary index the hook's git add writes to and git discards (index c6fbc485, HEAD and worktree both 56fc3b26). A MERGE commit could not carry it at all because pre-merge-commit runs after git has built the tree, so the regen only ever reached the index -- permanently dirty against HEAD, aborting the NEXT merge. And at 81f091af a clean textual merge spliced one side's manifest line with the other side's content, so main asserted d07a474f for a roadmap whose tree held 8dc68958 (1 stale of 423), with the merge driver configured and attributed but structurally unable to fire
fixed_by: 56fa71b5 + 89d86882: the file is untracked and pod_push.sh generates it from the HEAD it ships

supersedes_cause: a dirty runs/friction.jsonl or data/pod_head_manifest.txt aborts the merge
now_known: Half right and half wrong. The dirty-file abort is real -- git's pre-merge tree check runs BEFORE merge drivers, so a driver cannot help a file sitting dirty. But data/pod_head_manifest.txt was not dirty because someone left it dirty: the pre-merge-commit regen produced the dirt itself, so the abort was the previous merge's output, not an operator's untidiness. friction.jsonl's half is unchanged and is fixed by friction add --commit
fixed_by: 56fa71b5 (manifest untracked) + friction add --commit for the ledger half

supersedes_cause: after a three-way merge of b0-ve-rownorms the manifest sat staged-dirty
now_known: The staged-dirty state was pre-merge-commit's regen landing in the index after git had already built the merge tree -- index == worktree, HEAD different, the mirror of the path-scoped case, which is why post-commit's HEAD==worktree guard correctly declined to touch it
fixed_by: 56fa71b5: no regen in the hook at all

The arms will retrain with the MLA layers on model.py's SDPA explicit-mask path -- the reference that passed the control -- at whatever per-step cost that carries against the causal twins' 19s/10 steps. mask_mod stays usable for FORWARD-only work (eval, gates); scripts/n7c_grad_check.py is the check any future mask_mod training must pass.
